title: ConstraintTranslator: tokenizer-aware constraint translation for OpenAI-compat streaming and function-calling
author: Lina Park
release_notes: Introduce a tokenizer-aware ConstraintTranslator that maps high-level CFG/regex constraints into safe streaming-aware token-level constraints for OpenAI compatibility and function-calling; improves output correctness at token boundaries and adds integration tests and rollout flag.
description: Motivation: developers using OpenAI-compat streaming and function-calling modes saw intermittent structured-output breakage when constraints crossed tokenizer subtokens or when partial tokens were emitted during streaming. This PR introduces a ConstraintTranslator that bridges high-level CFG/regex constraints and the runtime's tokenizer-aware constrained-decoder backends. The translator produces framed, token-aligned constraint fragments and explicit prefix/postfix guards so the streaming decoder and KV/cache layers can maintain correctness without blocking low-latency emission. Design summary: 1) ConstraintTranslator takes a constraint AST (CFG or regex-backed) and the active tokenizer model to emit a set of token-span-safe constraint fragments, plus metadata for whether fragments are prefix-safe (can be applied mid-stream) or require lookbehind. 2) OpenAI compatibility layer now consults the translator when constraints are provided via the v1/outputs or tool-call paths; the compat layer will fall back to previous behavior if the translator flags an unsupported pattern. 3) Decoder changes: streaming framer was extended to accept fragment metadata to avoid emitting partial tokens that would invalidate regex/grammar matches; KV-cache semantics are adjusted to pin prefix fragments for correctness during canary rollouts. 4) Tool/function-calling: when a function signature or tool schema is enforced via structured-output constraints, the translator ensures argument boundaries align with tokenizer tokens and emits reconciliation hints so the tool-caller can parse partial streaming responses. Implementation notes: new module src/inference/constraint_translator.py with a compact tokenizer adapter, constraint normalizer, and fragmenter; re-use existing regex/CFG parsers under src/inference/constraints/*. The translator is feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.constraint_translator and off by default for Dedicated customers until compatibility testing completes. Tests & validation: extensive unit tests added under tests/constraint_translator/ covering edgecases for UTF-8 multi-byte tokens, emoji, and mixed-script inputs; integration tests simulate streaming with partial token emissions and tool-calling scenarios. Benchmarks: end-to-end latency measured with 1k requests showed median tail latency increase of +3ms and P99 +12ms when translator is enabled; malformed-output incidents in our structured-output regression suite dropped by ~85%. Rollout plan: behind FF for 2 weeks on staging, then progressive canary to 10% of hosted traffic, followed by full rollout; Dedicated customers can opt-in. Backwards compatibility: translator is additive; if a constraint cannot be translated safely the compat layer emits a structured warning and falls back to legacy rejection behavior. Migration notes: no changes required for callers; customers relying on precise token-level heuristics may observe improved stability.
